text:
Jin L: Heads-up — over the last 24h we've seen a subtle pattern: intermittent metadata CRC errors on nvme devices that only show up under heavy read bursts during GPU reclaim windows. Not yet a full failure but it's spiking attach latency.

Priya S: Can you link the nodes and a short log excerpt? Is this correlated with fstrim / overlayfs janitor runs?

Jin L: nodes: gnode-512, gnode-524, gnode-588 (all in us-east1-b). excerpt: `nvme0: I/O CRC error, metadata tag mismatch` repeated with read retries. iostat shows read ops concentrated on nvme0 while nvme1 idle.

Maria H: These filesystems are on our older 2TB drives with firmware v1.4.0 — we rolled a firmware batch last year but some stayed on the older image due to stuck upgrades. Could be a firmware edge case with concurrent discard/trimming.

Theo: If discard/fstrim hits during reclaim, controller may reorder meta updates causing CRC mismatches on retried reads. Short-term: disable fstrim on the affected pool for next 6 hours and stagger janitor waves.

Priya S: Risk: those drives are used for burst GPU provisioning (preemptible). If we disable fstrim and then a real bad block surfaces, we might see permanent corruption. What's the measured CRC rate?

Jin L: CRC rate ~0.08% over 1h on the three nodes, but read retries inflate latency causing attach pipeline to wait ~45-90s on some attaches. Not catastrophic but tail risk for customer-facing allocs.

infra-bot: alert: nvme_crc_spike region=us-east1-b nodes=3 window=60m rate=0.08%

Theo: Proposed mitigations (short): 1) Pause fstrim and deep-scrub on the affected hosts. 2) Reduce janitor concurrency for the us-east1-b shard to 20%. 3) Mark the three nodes as "avoid-new-attaches" while leaving current tasks running. 4) Add a fast-fail read-verify in the attach path that returns transient-degraded so provisioner can pick another host.

Priya S: Sounds good. What's the capacity impact? If we avoid those nodes we lose ~140 GPUs in the burst pool; attach SLOs for high-priority jobs will degrade but routing fallback to us-east2 is in place.

Maria H: I've started an S3 bucket for diagnostics: s3://redwood-debug/us-east1/aging-nvme/ with SMART dumps and controller logs. I'll also tag the drives for firmware upgrade scheduling (drive_firmware_upgrade backlog).

Jin L: After throttling janitor concurrency from 60% -> 20% the CRC alerts dropped ~70% within 30m and attach tail 95th improved from 110s -> 28s in our canary.

Priya S: Good. For long-term: schedule firmware cohort rolling for drives older than 14 months, add age-aware scrub windows (move to midnight low-iops), and add a health signal derived from read-latency + CRC-rate to preemptively retire drives before they impact provisioning. Add this as infra backlog items.

Theo: Also add a small improvement to the attach flow: early read-verify of the candidate device's headblock and return a quick transient-degraded decision if verification fails. Quick PR, low-risk.

infra-bot: mitigation_applied: janitor_concurrency_reduced host_filter=us-east1-b avoid_new_attaches_tagged diagnostics_bucket_created

Priya S: I'll open the lifecycle task and assign firmware rollout to the storage squad. Jin/THEO — please post a 2-bullet summary to #postmortems once stable (what happened, immediate mitigations).

Jin L: Will do. Monitoring for 6 more hours then decide on node drains. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
